title: The Pale Signal
premise: Sable Marchetti, the fourth clone of a woman murdered thirty years ago, works the courier lanes between two star fleets that nearly destroyed each other in the Armistice Wars. When a manifest lists her original's killer—dead for decades—as a passenger aboard a ship that never launched, Sable realizes the peace between the fleets rests on a forged signal she inherited, and someone is now unmaking it. To keep the lie alive, she must impersonate her dead original, walk into the heart of the fleet that killed her, and decide whether the peace built on her predecessor's sacrifice is worth her own identity. In the end, Sable broadcasts the truth herself, ending the fragile truce but forcing both fleets to finally speak—and choosing, for the first time, a name that is entirely her own.
about_author: Ansel Vasquez is the pen name of a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent eleven years routing cargo between hostile colonies before turning to fiction. They write about the people who keep impossible systems running, and what those systems cost them.

chapters.title: Long Route
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs a routine courier jump between the Concord fleet's hub and the derelict relay stations, establishing her solitary life, her careful anonymity, and her habit of never reading her original's case files. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a low hum of dread—she knows clones who read their files don't last.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A customs audit flags an anomaly: the name Edric Voss—her original's convicted killer, executed thirty years ago—appears on the manifest of the Pale Signal, a ship that never flew. She pulls her original's case file against every instinct. Emotional beat: the first crack in her invisibility, curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Dead Signed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with an intercut of her original's final recorded testimony. The file reveals the Armistice was sealed by a forged distress signal from the Pale Signal—a ship built only to die, crewed by clones of the original Marchetti. Emotional beat: horror and vertigo as Sable realizes her existence is a component of a peace treaty.

chapters.title: Concord Station
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She reports the anomaly to her Concord handler, Ade Osei, and watches him lie smoothly about a ship that officially never existed. Someone has already searched her quarters. Emotional beat: betrayal—the institution that made her is hunting her, and her invisibility is gone.

chapters.title: The Other Fleet
chapters.summary: Ilsa Reyes' POV, a Meridian fleet intelligence officer who has spent years chasing the Pale Signal myth. Ilsa intercepts Sable at a neutral port, not to arrest her but to offer a deal: help me expose the forgery before my fleet's hawks use it to restart the war. Emotional beat: wary, electric alliance between two women used as instruments.

chapters.title: Impostor
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. To access the Pale Signal's sealed black box, Sable must pass biometric gates keyed to her original—wearing her dead predecessor's identity, voice, and memories she's only read about. The box reveals Voss never fired the shot; the original Marchetti did, to create a martyr. Emotional beat: identity dissolution, grief for a woman she was built to replace.

chapters.title: Hawks
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Meridian hardliners, tipped by a leak from Osei, seize the black box data and prepare a first strike, framing Sable as a Concord saboteur. Ilsa must choose between her fleet and the truth. Emotional beat: the corruption of power laid bare—institutions devouring their own to preserve the lie.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable and Ilsa reach the Pale Signal's actual hull, drifting in a decommissioned shipyard, and find the last clone—Marchetti-3—alive in cryostasis for thirty years, kept as a living key. She wakes, recognizes Sable, and asks only: did it hold? Emotional beat: devastating tenderness between versions of one woman.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Ilsa POV. With Meridian strike wings launching, Sable hijacks the fleet-wide relay and transmits everything: the forged signal, the clone program, Voss's innocence, Marchetti-3's testimony. The strike falters; crews refuse orders built on a lie. Emotional beat: the climax—truth as an act of self-destruction and liberation at once.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, months later. The Armistice has collapsed into open, grinding negotiation—painful, honest, survivable. Marchetti-3 has chosen retirement; Sable has chosen a new name, new papers, a short route she picked herself. Osei faces tribunal; the fleets talk. Emotional beat: hard-won peace with the price paid—the cost of survival was her old self, and she doesn't miss it.
